question: Should OpenClaw expose an operator-controlled Control UI iframe allowlist, accepting the deliberate relaxation of default anti-framing headers for explicitly trusted origins?
rationale: The request introduces a new public configuration surface that changes a browser security boundary; code inspection cannot determine whether an existing supported integration or maintainer decision already resolves that policy question.

options.title: Approve a strict allowlist
options.body: Add a validated `controlUi.frameAncestors` setting that defaults to the current deny behavior and omits XFO only when embedding is explicitly enabled.

options.title: Keep Control UI non-embeddable
options.body: Retain the current anti-framing policy and direct operators to independently owned reverse-proxy deployment controls.

options.title: Defer for security design
options.body: Keep the request open until maintainers define allowed CSP syntax, supported browser behavior, and the intended embedded-session trust model.

recommendation.title: Approve a strict allowlist
recommendation.body: Add a validated `controlUi.frameAncestors` setting that defaults to the current deny behavior and omits XFO only when embedding is explicitly enabled.

likelyOwner.reason: Current Control UI and configuration-history ownership could not be traced under the unavailable command sandbox.
